subject: Sparrow Financial — sudden p99 latency and 5xx surge after qprofile v2.1 flip
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@sparrowfin.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: Kelsey Rivera <kelsey.rivera@sparrowfin.com>
Date: Sat, 02 Sep 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Sharp production latencies and 5xx after qprofile v2.1 swap

Neha,

We just flipped to Redwood qprofile v2.1 on our production pool at 15:50 PDT and immediately started seeing p99 jump from 420ms to 2.8s and a steady stream of 5xx errors across our high-volume routes. This is affecting our payment authorization flow and choking downstream queues.

We've attached a small trace and a tar of logs from the last 40 minutes. Can you confirm rollback options? This needs executive attention — our CSO is asking for mitigation and a credit/compensation estimate.

Attachments: perf_dump_20280902.tar.gz, cdf_trace_qprofile_v2.1.txt

- Amit Shah
VP Engineering, Sparrow Financial
amit.shah@sparrowfin.com

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@sparrowfin.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 02 Sep 2028 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sharp production latencies and 5xx after qprofile v2.1 swap

Amit —

Thanks for the heads-up and for sending the logs. We've started triage. Initial telemetry shows a sudden increase in token decode retries on the GPU hosts serving that fleet + elevated tail memory pressure coincident with the qprofile flip. Marcus is running a fast assessment on rollback safety.

Immediate plan:
- Marcus: confirm whether a safe quick rollback is possible without warmup artifacts (target ETA 30m).
- Laura: open a billing/credits note and prepare an initial estimate for customer impact window.
- I'll request an exec bridge if rollback isn't clean within 45m.

Please stand by; I will update every 30 minutes.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 02 Sep 2028 16:39:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sharp production latencies and 5xx after qprofile v2.1 swap

Neha / team —

Quick update from infra: the qprofile v2.1 variant that deployed includes a tighter int8 packing path which reduces memory footprint but appears to trigger suboptimal kernel selection for sequences >1024 on T4-like hardware in their dedicated pool. That explains the p99 spike and the sporadic 5xx (OOM/retry) behavior.

Rollback notes:
- We can roll them back to qprofile v2.0 immediately via the routing layer with per-zone cutover; estimated mitigation start in ~20 minutes if we proceed now.
- Risk: clients using pinned model variants might see short tail errors during cutover — we'll coordinate graceful drain.

I recommend rollback now and a postmortem to validate the qprofile heuristics across their seq distribution. Creating a runbook entry in SUP-9217.

-Marcus
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@sparrowfin.com>, Kelsey Rivera <kelsey.rivera@sparrowfin.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 02 Sep 2028 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sharp production latencies and 5xx after qprofile v2.1 swap

Amit / Kelsey —

We are rolling your fleet back to qprofile v2.0 now. Marcus' team will execute a per-zone routing rollback; expected mitigation window ~20-30 minutes, during which you may see intermittent 5xx while connections drain. We'll monitor p99 and error rate and pause the rollback if we detect anomalous regressions.

Laura is preparing an impact summary + estimate for credits; Jonas is standing by to loop in support engineering for deeper trace correlation.

I'll send a status update when rollback completes. Very sorry for the disruption.

-Neha

From: Kelsey Rivera <kelsey.rivera@sparrowfin.com>

Our security/compliance team is asking for a short exec-level summary they can present to the board. Can Redwood provide a concise timeline and root-cause statement (non-technical summary) and a proposed credit range for the impacted window?

Kelsey
Director of Reliability, Sparrow Financial

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@sparrowfin.com>, Kelsey Rivera <kelsey.rivera@sparrowfin.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 03 Sep 2028 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sharp production latencies and 5xx after qprofile v2.1 swap — executive brief and next steps

Amit / Kelsey —

Executive summary (for board):
- What happened: On 2028-09-02 15:50 PDT, Sparrow's fleet was switched to Redwood quantization profile v2.1. Within minutes, we observed sustained p99 latency increases (from ~420ms to >2.5s) and a rise in 5xx errors impacting the auth/payment flows.
- Immediate cause: A kernel selection mismatch for sequences >1024 under qprofile v2.1 on Sparrow's current hardware profile caused memory pressure and decode retries, leading to increased tail latency and occasional OOMs.
- Impact window: 2028-09-02 15:50 PDT to 2028-09-02 17:10 PDT (rolling rollback completed and tail latency returned to baseline).
- Mitigation taken: Immediate rollback to qprofile v2.0 via routing layer; per-zone drains and increased autoscaling while rollback completed.
- Next steps: 1) Full postmortem correlating Sparrow’s sequence-length distribution with kernel heuristics (owner: Marcus Lin, ETA 72h); 2) Harden qprofile automated canary gate for seq distribution mismatches (owner: Runtime team); 3) Compensation proposal from Redwood (Laura to propose credit range; baseline estimate attached).

Attached: initial impact timeline and log summary.

We will follow up with a formal PM/SE postmortem and remediation plan by EOD Wednesday. Deep apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as high priority.

-Neha Kapoor
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments: sparrow_impact_summary_20280903.pdf (draft)
